**Fort Aguada** is a seventeenth-century [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire")-era [fort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort "Fort"), built in 1612, along with a lighthouse, standing in [Goa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goa "Goa"), India, on [Sinquerim Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinquerim "Sinquerim"), overlooking the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea"). It is an [ASI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeological_Survey_of_India "Archaeological Survey of India") protected [Monument of National Importance in Goa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Monuments_of_National_Importance_in_Goa "List of Monuments of National Importance in Goa").

## Origins and history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Origins and history")]

Aguada fort was originally constructed in 1612 to guard against the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Empire "Dutch Empire"). It was a reference point for the vessels coming from [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") at that time. This old Portuguese fort stands on the beach south of [Candolim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candolim "Candolim"), at the shore of the [Mandovi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandovi_River "Mandovi River"). It was initially tasked with defense of shipping and the nearby [Bardez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bardez "Bardez") sub-district.

A freshwater spring within the fort provided water supply to the ships that used to stop by. This is how the fort got its name: Aguada, meaning [watery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water "Water") in the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") language. Crews of passing ships would often visit to replenish their freshwater stores. The [Aguada Fort Lighthouse](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farol%20da%20Fortaleza%20da%20Aguada "pt:Farol da Fortaleza da Aguada") erected in 1864 is the oldest of its kind in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"). Built in 1612, it was once the grandstand of 79 [cannons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannon "Cannon"). It has the capacity of storing 2,376,000 [gallons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallon "Gallon") of water, one of the biggest freshwater storage of the time in whole of [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"). This fort is divided in two segments: the upper part acted as fort and watering station, while the lower part served as a safe berth for Portuguese [ships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship "Ship"). Whereas the upper part has a [moat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moat "Moat"), underground [water storage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_storage "Water storage") chamber, [gunpowder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunpowder "Gunpowder") room, [lighthouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse "Lighthouse"), and [bastions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastion "Bastion"), it also has a secret escape passage to use during time of war and emergency. The lighthouse at the initial stage used to emit light once in 7 minutes.

Fort Aguada was the most prized and crucial fort of [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_people "Portuguese people"). The fort is so large that it envelops the entire [peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsula "Peninsula") at the southwestern tip of [Bardez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bardez "Bardez"). Built on the mouth of [Mandovi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandovi_River "Mandovi River"), it was strategically located and was the chief defense of Portuguese against the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Empire "Dutch Empire").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-:0-1)

During the [Salazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_de_Oliveira_Salazar "António de Oliveira Salazar") Administration, Fort Aguada was repurposed for use as a prison primarily, some claim, for Salazar's political opponents.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Aguada lighthouse

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Aguada lighthouse")]

The Aguada lighthouse was built in 1864 on a hill located on the west to the fort. It is one of the oldest in Asia. It is located across the river from the peninsula encompassing Panaji and just south of Candolim beach. It was replaced by a new lighthouse in 1976 after serving for about a century. There was a large bell on the lighthouse which was found in the ruins of Saint Augustine monastery in Old Goa.It is an ideal place to visit.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-:0-1)

## Aguada Central Jail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Aguada Central Jail")]

The jail is a part of the fort and was the largest prison in Goa until 2015. The 17th-century Portuguese-era structure has been renovated by the Goa Tourism Development Corporation along with the Goa Heritage Action Group and Goa's freedom fighters and opened for tourists as a Freedom Struggle Museum to showcase Goa's freedom struggle and be a true tribute to the heroic deeds and glorious sacrifices of all those who took part in Goa's Liberation and who fought against the Portuguese rule and British rule for the freedom of India and were jailed there. It was inaugurated on December 19, 2021 by PM [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi"). The redevelopment cost approximately Rs 22 crore under the Centre's Swadesh Darshan Scheme. This museum has two particular cells dedicated to liberation fighters T B Cunha and Ram Manohar Lohia, where they were imprisoned under the Portuguese regime. This site also contains Portuguese cannons, and several monuments to Goa's anti-colonial struggle.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-6)

## Taj Fort Aguada Resort

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Taj Fort Aguada Resort")]

[Taj Fort Aguada Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Fort_Aguada_Resort "Taj Fort Aguada Resort") formerly Fort Aguada Beach Resort is part of [Taj Hotel Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Hotels "Taj Hotels"). The hotel opened in 1974 at the site of the historic Portuguese Fort Aguada.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-7)

**Fort Aguada** is a seventeenth-century [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire")-era [fort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort "Fort"), built in 1612, along with a lighthouse, standing in [Goa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goa "Goa"), India, on [Sinquerim Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinquerim "Sinquerim"), overlooking the [Arabian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea"). It is an [ASI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeological_Survey_of_India "Archaeological Survey of India") protected [Monument of National Importance in Goa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Monuments_of_National_Importance_in_Goa "List of Monuments of National Importance in Goa").

## Origins and history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Origins and history")]

Aguada fort was originally constructed in 1612 to guard against the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Empire "Dutch Empire"). It was a reference point for the vessels coming from [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") at that time. This old Portuguese fort stands on the beach south of [Candolim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candolim "Candolim"), at the shore of the [Mandovi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandovi_River "Mandovi River"). It was initially tasked with defense of shipping and the nearby [Bardez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bardez "Bardez") sub-district.

A freshwater spring within the fort provided water supply to the ships that used to stop by. This is how the fort got its name: Aguada, meaning [watery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water "Water") in the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") language. Crews of passing ships would often visit to replenish their freshwater stores. The [Aguada Fort Lighthouse](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farol%20da%20Fortaleza%20da%20Aguada "pt:Farol da Fortaleza da Aguada") erected in 1864 is the oldest of its kind in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"). Built in 1612, it was once the grandstand of 79 [cannons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannon "Cannon"). It has the capacity of storing 2,376,000 [gallons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallon "Gallon") of water, one of the biggest freshwater storage of the time in whole of [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"). This fort is divided in two segments: the upper part acted as fort and watering station, while the lower part served as a safe berth for Portuguese [ships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship "Ship"). Whereas the upper part has a [moat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moat "Moat"), underground [water storage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_storage "Water storage") chamber, [gunpowder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunpowder "Gunpowder") room, [lighthouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse "Lighthouse"), and [bastions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastion "Bastion"), it also has a secret escape passage to use during time of war and emergency. The lighthouse at the initial stage used to emit light once in 7 minutes.

Fort Aguada was the most prized and crucial fort of [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_people "Portuguese people"). The fort is so large that it envelops the entire [peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsula "Peninsula") at the southwestern tip of [Bardez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bardez "Bardez"). Built on the mouth of [Mandovi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandovi_River "Mandovi River"), it was strategically located and was the chief defense of Portuguese against the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Empire "Dutch Empire").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-:0-1)

During the [Salazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_de_Oliveira_Salazar "António de Oliveira Salazar") Administration, Fort Aguada was repurposed for use as a prison primarily, some claim, for Salazar's political opponents.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Aguada lighthouse

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Aguada lighthouse")]

The Aguada lighthouse was built in 1864 on a hill located on the west to the fort. It is one of the oldest in Asia. It is located across the river from the peninsula encompassing Panaji and just south of Candolim beach. It was replaced by a new lighthouse in 1976 after serving for about a century. There was a large bell on the lighthouse which was found in the ruins of Saint Augustine monastery in Old Goa.It is an ideal place to visit.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-:0-1)

## Aguada Central Jail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Aguada Central Jail")]

The jail is a part of the fort and was the largest prison in Goa until 2015. The 17th-century Portuguese-era structure has been renovated by the Goa Tourism Development Corporation along with the Goa Heritage Action Group and Goa's freedom fighters and opened for tourists as a Freedom Struggle Museum to showcase Goa's freedom struggle and be a true tribute to the heroic deeds and glorious sacrifices of all those who took part in Goa's Liberation and who fought against the Portuguese rule and British rule for the freedom of India and were jailed there. It was inaugurated on December 19, 2021 by PM [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi"). The redevelopment cost approximately Rs 22 crore under the Centre's Swadesh Darshan Scheme. This museum has two particular cells dedicated to liberation fighters T B Cunha and Ram Manohar Lohia, where they were imprisoned under the Portuguese regime. This site also contains Portuguese cannons, and several monuments to Goa's anti-colonial struggle.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-6)

## Taj Fort Aguada Resort

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fort_Aguada&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Taj Fort Aguada Resort")]

[Taj Fort Aguada Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Fort_Aguada_Resort "Taj Fort Aguada Resort") formerly Fort Aguada Beach Resort is part of [Taj Hotel Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Hotels "Taj Hotels"). The hotel opened in 1974 at the site of the historic Portuguese Fort Aguada.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Aguada#cite_note-7)

**Afonso de Albuquerque, 1st Duke of Goa** (c.1453 – 16 December 1515), was a Portuguese general, admiral, statesman, and _[conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")_. He served as [viceroy of Portuguese India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Portuguese_India "List of governors of Portuguese India") from 1509 to 1515, during which he expanded Portuguese influence across the Indian Ocean and built a reputation as a fierce and skilled military commander.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Albuquerque_p._1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-3)

Albuquerque advanced the three-fold Portuguese grand scheme of combating [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam"), spreading [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"), and securing the trade of spices by establishing a Portuguese Asian empire.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-4) Among his achievements, Albuquerque managed to conquer [Goa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goa "Goa") and was the first European of the [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance "Renaissance") to raid the [Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf"), and he led the first voyage by a European fleet into the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-5) He is generally considered a highly effective military commander,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Foundations-6) and "probably the greatest naval commander of the age",[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-7) given his successful strategy of attempting to close all the Indian Ocean naval passages to the Atlantic, Red Sea, Persian Gulf, and to the Pacific, transforming it into a Portuguese _[mare clausum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mare\_clausum "Mare clausum")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Chisholm-8) He was appointed head of the "fleet of the Arabian and Persian sea" in 1506.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Iranica-9)

Many of the conflicts in which he was directly involved took place in the Indian Ocean, in the Persian Gulf regions for control of the trade routes, and on the coasts of India. His military brilliance in these initial campaigns enabled Portugal to become the first global empire in history.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-10) He led the Portuguese forces in numerous battles, including the [conquest of Goa in 1510](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Conquest_of_Goa_(1510) "Portuguese Conquest of Goa (1510)") and the [capture of Malacca in 1511](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capture_of_Malacca_(1511) "Capture of Malacca (1511)").

During the last five years of his life, he turned to administration,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBandelier1907-11) where his actions as the second governor of [Portuguese India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_India "Portuguese India") were crucial to the longevity of the Portuguese Empire. He oversaw expeditions that resulted in establishing diplomatic contacts with the [Ayutthaya Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayutthaya_Kingdom "Ayutthaya Kingdom") through his envoy [Duarte Fernandes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duarte_Fernandes "Duarte Fernandes"), with [Pegu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanthawaddy_Kingdom "Hanthawaddy Kingdom") in Myanmar, and [Timor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timor "Timor") and the [Moluccas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maluku_Islands "Maluku Islands") through a voyage headed by [António de Abreu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_de_Abreu "António de Abreu") and [Francisco Serrão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Serr%C3%A3o "Francisco Serrão"). He laid the path for European trade with [Ming China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_China "Ming China") through [Rafael Perestrello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Perestrello "Rafael Perestrello"). He also aided in establishing [diplomatic relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateus_(ambassador) "Mateus (ambassador)") with [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Empire "Ethiopian Empire"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-14) and [established diplomatic ties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese%E2%80%93Safavid_relations "Portuguese–Safavid relations") with Persia during the [Safavid dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safavid_dynasty "Safavid dynasty").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-15)

Throughout his career, he received epithets such as "the Terrible",[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-16) "the Great",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Albuquerque_p._1-2) "the Lion of the Seas",[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Albuquerque-17) "the Portuguese Mars",[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Chisholm-8) and "the Caesar of the East".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Albuquerque-17)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Afonso_de_Albuquerque&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Afonso de Albuquerque was born in 1453 in [Alhandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vila_Franca_de_Xira "Vila Franca de Xira"), near Lisbon.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-18) He was the second son of Gonçalo de Albuquerque, Lord of Vila Verde dos Francos, and Dona Leonor de Menezes. His father held an important position at court and was connected by remote illegitimate descent with the Portuguese monarchy. He was a descendant of [King Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_of_Portugal "Denis of Portugal")'s illegitimate son, [Afonso Sanches, Lord of Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_Sanches,_Lord_of_Albuquerque "Afonso Sanches, Lord of Albuquerque"). He was educated in mathematics and Latin at the court of [Afonso V of Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_V_of_Portugal "Afonso V of Portugal"), where he befriended Prince John, the future King [John II of Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_of_Portugal "John II of Portugal").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStephens1897-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Jayne-20)

## Early military service, 1471–1509

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Afonso_de_Albuquerque&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early military service, 1471–1509")]

In 1471, under the command of Afonso V, he was present at the conquest of [Tangier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangier "Tangier") and [Arzila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquest_of_Asilah "Conquest of Asilah") in Morocco,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-britannica.com-21) and he served there as an officer for some years. In 1476, he accompanied [Prince John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_of_Portugal "John II of Portugal") in wars against Castile, including the [Battle of Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Toro "Battle of Toro"). He participated in the campaign on the Italian peninsula in 1480 to assist [Ferdinand I of Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Naples "Ferdinand I of Naples") in repelling the [Ottoman invasion of Otranto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_invasion_of_Otranto "Ottoman invasion of Otranto").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBandelier1907-11) On his return in 1481, when John was crowned as King John II, Albuquerque was made [master of the horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_the_Horse "Master of the Horse") and chief [equerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equerry "Equerry") (_\_estribeiro-mor\__) to the king, a post which he held throughout John's reign.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-britannica.com-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Jayne-20) In 1489, he returned to military campaigning in North Africa, as commander of defense in the [Graciosa fortress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graciosa_fortress "Graciosa fortress"), an island in the river Luco near the city of [Larache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larache "Larache"). In 1490 Albuquerque was part of the guard of John II. He returned to Arzila in 1495, where his younger brother Martim died fighting by his side.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### First expedition to India, 1503

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Afonso_de_Albuquerque&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: First expedition to India, 1503")]

Main article: [5th Portuguese India Armada (Albuquerque, 1503)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5th_Portuguese_India_Armada_(Albuquerque,_1503) "5th Portuguese India Armada (Albuquerque, 1503)")

When King [Manuel I of Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_I_of_Portugal "Manuel I of Portugal") ascended to the throne following the death of his cousin [John II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_of_Portugal "John II of Portugal"), he held a cautious attitude towards Albuquerque, who was a close friend of his predecessor and seventeen years Manuel's senior. Eight years later, on 6 April 1503 Albuquerque was sent on his first expedition to India together with his cousin Francisco de Albuquerque. Each commanded three ships, sailing with [Duarte Pacheco Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duarte_Pacheco_Pereira "Duarte Pacheco Pereira") and [Nicolau Coelho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolau_Coelho "Nicolau Coelho"). They engaged in several battles against the forces of the [Zamorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamorin "Zamorin") of [Calicut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kozhikode "Kozhikode") (_Calecute_, Kozhikode) and succeeded in establishing the [king](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Cochin "Kingdom of Cochin") of [Cochin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi,_India "Kochi, India") (_Cochim_, Kochi) securely on his throne. In return, the king of Cochin gave the Portuguese permission to build the Portuguese [fort _Immanuel_ (Fort Kochi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Emmanuel "Fort Emmanuel") and establish trade relations with [Quilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quilon "Quilon") (_Coulão_, [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam")). This laid the foundation for the eastern [Portuguese Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_de_Albuquerque#cite_note-Chisholm-8)

## Second expedition to India, 1506–1509

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Afonso_de_Albuquerque&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Second expedition to India, 1506–1509")]

### Return, 1506

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Afonso_de_Albuquerque&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return, 1506")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Southeast_Asia_Portuguese_Empire_1.png/330px-Southeast_Asia_Portuguese_Empire_1.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Southeast_Asia_Portuguese_Empire_1.png)
